summary_en: This study tests moderately hypofractionated, MR-guided adaptive pelvic intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) given as adjuvant treatment for endometrial cancer. The radiation is delivered by an MR-linac in a total dose of 42 Gy over 15 fractions, with daily MRI guidance and plan adjustments as needed, and vaginal brachytherapy may follow at the physician's discretion. The study aims to evaluate safety, tolerability and preliminary efficacy.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radioterapia pélvica de intensidad modulada (IMRT) adaptativa guiada por resonancia magnética, con dosis moderadamente hipofraccionada, como tratamiento adyuvante para el cáncer de endometrio. La radiación se administra con un equipo MR-linac, en una dosis total de 42 Gy en 15 fracciones, con resonancia magnética diaria y ajustes del plan según sea necesario; la braquiterapia vaginal puede aplicarse después, a criterio del médico. El estudio busca evaluar la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la eficacia preliminar.
who_for: Confirmed endometrial carcinoma of an eligible type (endometrioid, serous, clear cell, carcinosarcoma or dedifferentiated).
Indication for adjuvant pelvic radiation based on ASTRO and GOG-99 high-intermediate-risk features.
Age 18 or older and able to give informed consent.
Eligible for adjuvant systemic therapy if needed, with at least 3 weeks between chemotherapy and radiation.
Willing and able to complete the EORTC QLQ-C30 and EN-24 questionnaires in a validated language.
not_for: Contraindication to pelvic radiotherapy, such as active connective tissue disorder or inflammatory bowel disease.
Hip prosthesis that would compromise treatment planning or delivery.
